facts.text: On this date in 1869, the Suez Canal opened to navigation — cutting the London-to-Bombay sea route by 7,000 kilometers and immediately reshaping which cities became wealthy.
More people live within a 24-hour train ride of Tokyo than in the entire continent of North America.
On this date in 1917, the Balfour Declaration was issued — a 67-word letter that helped determine the borders of the modern Middle East.
Mongolia has a lower population density than any sovereign nation on Earth except Greenland, averaging fewer than 2 people per square kilometer across a country twice the size of Texas.
The city of Chongqing, China, has more registered residents than Australia, Canada, and New Zealand combined.
On this day in 1979, Chrysler asked the U.S. government for $1.5 billion in loan guarantees. Congress said yes. The company repaid early and the Treasury turned a profit.
On this day in 1860, Lincoln's election triggered an immediate market panic in Southern states — cotton futures in New Orleans dropped 10% before he even took office.
The S&P 500 has historically risen more in the 12 months after a U.S. presidential election than in any other 12-month window in a 4-year cycle.
Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway started as a failing textile mill. Buffett later called buying it the worst trade of his life — it cost him roughly $200 billion in opportunity loss.
The Dutch East India Company, the first publicly traded corporation, was so dominant it accounted for roughly 1.5% of global GDP at its peak — no single company has come close since.
On this day in 1572, Tycho Brahe observed a new star in Cassiopeia — a supernova so bright it was visible in daylight. It shattered the ancient belief that the heavens were eternal and unchanging.

Your bones are not static scaffolding. Every decade, your entire skeleton is replaced, osteoclasts dissolving old bone while osteoblasts rebuild it — you are literally not the same person you were ten years ago.
On this day in 1860, Abraham Lincoln was elected president without appearing on the ballot in ten Southern states. His name was simply not printed.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Tardigrades survive the vacuum of open space, not by being tough — but by entering cryptobiosis, halting all metabolism and becoming, for practical purposes, temporarily not alive.
On this day in 1860, Lincoln was elected president without appearing on the ballot in ten Southern states. He won anyway.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded.
On this day in 1917, the Bolshevik Revolution began — the entire Soviet era, from Lenin to Gorbachev, fits inside a single human lifespan.
The fax machine was invented in 1843, twenty-three years before the first transatlantic telegraph cable was successfully laid.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid.
Saudade (Portuguese): a melancholic longing for something beloved and gone. Linguists consider it untranslatable — the word itself is the feeling made solid.
Hiraeth (Welsh): homesickness for a home you cannot return to, or one that never existed. It carries grief, yearning, and belonging collapsed into eight letters.
Mamihlapinatapai (Yaghan): the shared glance between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. The language it comes from, spoken in Tierra del Fuego, is now effectively extinct.

On this date in 1860, Abraham Lincoln won the U.S. presidency — and the word 'rail-splitter,' his campaign nickname, briefly entered common use as a synonym for a self-made man before vanishing entirely.
On this date in 1917, the Bolshevik Revolution began — giving the world 'agitprop,' compressed from agitatsiya propaganda, a portmanteau so efficient it outlasted the ideology that coined it.

On Nov 6, 2013, Bitcoin crossed $200 for the first time — then hit $1,000 within four weeks. The move was driven largely by Chinese retail demand via BTC China, then the world's highest-volume exchange.
On Nov 6, 2010, the Bitcoin forum user 'ribuck' proposed the term 'satoshi' for 0.00000001 BTC. It took two more years before the denomination was formally adopted by the community.
Ethereum's gas limit is not fixed in protocol — miners and validators vote it up or down each block by a small margin, making throughput a rolling social consensus rather than a hard rule.
The Bitcoin UTXO set — every unspent coin output ever created — fits entirely in RAM on a modern laptop. As of 2026 it remains under 12 GB, a deliberately engineered property of the UTXO model.

Satoshi's known addresses hold roughly 1.1 million BTC, none of which has ever moved. On-chain analysis identifies them by the Patoshi pattern: a distinctive nonce-extrapolation signature in early block headers.
On this date in 2017, DeepMind's AlphaGo Zero was published — it learned Go from scratch with zero human data, defeating the version that beat Lee Sedol 100 games to 0 within 40 days of self-play.
On this date in 2022, Meta released Galactica, a 120B-parameter science LLM. It was pulled offline after 72 hours when users found it confidently fabricated citations, dosages, and historical facts.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of about 4,500 average US households.
The first neural network to defeat a human champion at a board game was TD-Gammon in 1992, trained purely through self-play using temporal-difference reinforcement learning on a 40-node hidden layer.

Transformers, now the dominant architecture in AI, were introduced in a 2017 paper by eight Google Brain authors — six of whom left Google within five years to found or co-found competing AI companies.
